reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Shane Legg from 2018 that I could quote from a page I actually opened.

- **The likely source:** On 16 May 2018 the University of Waikato posted a video of Legg's Distinguished Alumni Award lecture, titled "Where is Artificial General Intelligence taking us? ... My journey so far." It probably contains forecasts about when AGI arrives. But YouTube served a bot-protection page, so I could only see the title, upload date and description. There was no transcript. Watching that video is the obvious next step if you want to check the year further.
- **Other 2018 pages:** A Hacker News comment from 20 December 2018 mentions his "AGI at 2028" forecast. Those are a commenter's words linking to his 2011 blog post, not Legg speaking in 2018. One of his 2018 tweets showed up only inside a search snippet of someone else's reply. It was study advice, not a prediction.
- **His well-known forecasts come from other years:** The search results point to his 2011 LessWrong Q&A, his 2021 tweet repeating "50% by 2028 and 90% by 2040", and 2023 and 2025 interviews. I only saw these in search snippets and did not open them, so they are listed for checking, not confirmed.

Two problems with the run: two pages would not give usable text (the YouTube video and the Waikato alumni page, which was blocked). The Waikato 2018 annual report PDF did open, but because of a slip in my code I never read its text. All 12 searches were used and each ran once. I used 5 of the 6 page openings. `quiet_year` is true because all the fixed searches ran and no candidate turned up.
